title: Social media use and early adolescent brain structure: Findings from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study
authors: Nagata JM, Bao K, Murray SB, Nedelec P, Richardson RA, Nayak S, Li EJ, Wong JH, Muller-Oehring EM, Scheffler A, Baker FC, Rauschecker AM, Sugrue LP

primary_models.name: Generalized additive mixed model (gamm4) of z-scored ROI cortical thickness on daily social media hours or social media addiction score, adjusted for demographics, SES, genetic ancestry, non-SM screen time and scanner, family random effect
primary_models.location_in_paper: Table 2 (p. 4) for all ROI cortical thickness estimates; Fig. 1 (p. 5) plots the same social media time coefficients; right-hemisphere cortical volume estimate in Results 3.1 text (p. 4). Methods 2.4 and 2.6.1 (p. 3); interpreted in Discussion pp. 6-7.
primary_models.design: Cross-sectional. Social media use, social media addiction, and structural MRI all come from the ABCD Year 2 follow-up visit (2018-2020, ages 10-13). One observation per participant. Social media time and social media addiction were entered in separate models (Spearman rho = 0.67 between them) to avoid collinearity. Each ROI-by-hemisphere measure is a separate dependent variable; the paper also fit the same models to cortical surface area, cortical volume and subcortical volume ROIs, but only the thickness results are tabulated.
primary_models.sample: ABCD Study 6.0 release, Year 2 visit, 21 U.S. sites. Of 10,973 participants, 8,059 had sMRI, 7,866 passed the ABCD recommended imaging inclusion criteria, and 7,614 remained after removing missing covariates (age, sex, race, caregiver partnership, household income, caregiver education, non-SM screen time, genetic ancestry). Mean age 12.0 (SD 0.7); 53.3% male, 46.7% female. Race: White 69.0%, Black 14.1%, more than one race 11.0%, Asian 1.8%, Native American/Alaska Native 0.5%, Native Hawaiian/Pacific Islander 0.2%, other/not reported 3.4%. Household income: 31.7% $100,000-$199,999, 12.8% >= $200,000, 10.0% <= $24,999. Caregiver education: 33.4% graduate/professional degree. 75.1% partnered caregivers.
primary_models.iv: Two IVs, each in its own model. (1) Social media time: ABCD Youth Screen Time Survey item asking hours and minutes per day on social media (e.g., Instagram, Facebook, Twitter), reported separately for a typical weekday and weekend day; daily average = (weekday*5 + weekend*2)/7; 14 participants winsorized at 16 h/day. Mean 0.6 h/day (SD 1.5) (Table 1). (2) Social media addiction: six-item Social Media Addiction Questionnaire adapted from the Bergen Facebook Addiction Scale, 1 (Never) to 6 (Very often), averaged across items; youth with no social media account assigned 1. Mean 1.4 (SD 0.8) (Table 1). The paper describes the coefficients as standardized betas; whether the IV itself was z-scored is not stated explicitly in Methods.
primary_models.dv: FreeSurfer 7.1.1 (ABCD 6.0 tabulated data) cortical thickness for the 34 Desikan-Killiany ROIs in each hemisphere plus whole-hemisphere 'All Cortical Gray Matter' thickness, z-scored (Table 2 column header: 'mean z-scored thickness'). One further in-text estimate uses right-hemisphere total cortical volume. Surface area, other volume and subcortical volume ROI results are not printed.

primary_models.equation: z_thickness_ROI,hemi[i] = b0 + b1*SM[i] + b2*age + b3*sex + b4..*race + b..*PC1..PC10 + b*caregiver_partnership + b..*income + b..*caregiver_education + b*nonSM_screen_time + b..*scanner_serial + b..*scanner_software + u_family(i) + e[i], where SM is either daily social media hours or social media addiction score (separate models). Table 2 reports 100*b1 (standardized).
primary_models.estimation: R 4.4.2, gamm4 package (generalized additive mixed model); family ID random effect. No survey weights reported. Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction across ROIs; significance in Table 2 shown at Q < 0.05 (dark shading), with raw p < 0.05 shown in light shading. No interaction or stratified analyses. Sensitivity analysis adding CBCL ADHD T-score as a covariate reported only for vertexwise maps (Supplemental Figure A.3, not in this PDF); authors state the ROI relationships persisted after adjusting for ADHD score (Discussion p. 7) but no numbers are printed. A complementary vertexwise FEMA analysis (MATLAB R2025a) with the same fixed and random effects is shown only as Z-score maps (Fig. 2).

d_transformation.native_metric: Standardized beta x 100 (beta_std scaled by 100), with SEM
d_transformation.conversion_formula: beta_std = value / 100; treat beta_std as approximate r; d = 2*beta_std / sqrt(1 - beta_std^2) (Borenstein et al. 2009). If coders determine the IV was not standardized (i.e., coefficient is change in z-thickness per 1 h/day or per 1 SMAQ point), use beta_std = (value/100) * SD_IV / SD_DV with SD_DV = 1.
d_transformation.contrast_type: per 1 SD of the social media variable (assuming fully standardized beta)
d_transformation.notes: Only SE (SEM) is printed, no CIs, so d CIs cannot be derived without computing from SE (not done here). DV is z-scored thickness (SD_DV = 1 by construction, Table 2 header). SD_IV from Table 1 (p. 3): social media time SD = 1.5 h/day; SMAQ SD = 0.8. The paper calls these 'standardized beta coefficients' (Results p. 4, Fig. 1 caption, Discussion p. 7: 'standardized beta coefficients ... ranged from -0.051 to -0.026'), consistent with a fully standardized metric, but Methods do not state the IV was z-scored. All effects are small (|beta_std| <= 0.051).

extraction_flags: 916, SE 0.931, p = 0.040). Things to check: (1) Table 2 is an image; I read it from a 400-dpi render and spot-checked several cells, but all 140 values should be checked by a human against p. 4. (2) Values are stored as printed (x100 standardized beta), so they need to be divided by 100 before conversion. The paper calls them standardized betas, but Methods never say the IV was z-scored. If it was not, the coefficient is change in z-thickness per hour/day or per SMAQ point, and you should use sd_iv (1.5 / 0.8 from Table 1). The d conversion depends on this. (3) Only SE is reported, no CIs, so value_lo and value_hi are null. (4) For the 'All Cortical Gray Matter' rows only a raw p is printed (no FDR q), and the same is true for the right-hemisphere volume estimate. I set sig=true from raw p < 0.05. The text is ambiguous on whether the volume result was FDR-corrected, and it cites Table 2 even though Table 2 only shows thickness. (5) Social media time is significant at q<0.05 in 37 ROI cells, plus 2 whole-hemisphere cells and 1 volume cell. No social media addiction cell is significant. (6) Excluded: the vertexwise FEMA results (Z-maps only), the ADHD-covariate sensitivity analysis (narrative or figure only), and the surface area / subcortical volume ROI results (narrative only; supplement not bundled in the PDF). If the online supplement has those tables, they may add estimates. (7) Site is not a listed covariate; only scanner serial number and software version are.
